study_identification_part.si4_title: Neurodevelopmental model of schizophrenia revisited: similarity in individual deviation and idiosyncrasy from the normative model of whole-brain white matter tracts and shared brain-cognition covariation with ADHD and ASD

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Map deviations from normative ranges of whole-brain white matter tracts at the individual level to compare schizophrenia (by stage) with ASD and ADHD, and assess shared brain–cognition covariation.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The number of typically developing controls (TDC) is explicitly stated in the Participants section of the main text.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: This study recruited 281 patients with schizophrenia (aged 16 -40 yrs), 175 children and adults with ASD (9 -35 yrs), 279 children and adults with ADHD (7 -38 yrs), and 626 typically developing controls (TDC) (Table 1 and STable 1 -2).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: WM tract deviation and idiosyncrasy patterns are similar between early-stage schizophrenia and ASD/ADHD, with similarity diminishing in chronic schizophrenia.
